findings.gap: The goal verifier allowed a child-WI push plan to replace the end-to-end WI-548 parent objective and declare success without merge, WI-553, G7, or parent closeout.
findings.why_general: Any long Grok/Cursor run can narrow its generated plan after a review or compaction; the current wave validator runs only after the agent already decides to claim that a batch is closing and is not bound to an immutable root objective.
findings.harness_fix: Extend _shared/session-contract.md and the route-workflow prompt composer with immutable original_objective, objective_root_wi, required_wis, and terminal_condition fields; make the Grok /goal verifier and hooks/svc-task-completion-guard.sh reject a narrower plan or final response unless an owner-approved goal-change record exists, and automatically run scripts/validate-wave-closeout.mjs over required_wis.

findings.gap: The harness kept the multi-WI program in one 14-hour Grok context through six compactions instead of isolating WIs and chain stages.
findings.why_general: The shipped route contract explicitly limits fresh stage subagents to Claude and leaves non-Claude hosts on the prose chain, so the next Grok parent program will again accumulate unrelated WI state, tool output, and closeout obligations in one degrading context.
findings.harness_fix: Extend scripts/stage-segment.mjs and the Stage-context isolation block in skills/route-workflow/SKILL.md to Grok and Cursor: one WI/stage per fresh governed child, a hash-bound stage baton, receipt verification before return, and no prose-summary authority across compaction boundaries.

findings.gap: Grok-to-Cursor mutation handoff did not normalize the real Grok session identity or create a releasable delegated child claim, leaving WI-553 owned by a dead synthetic session.
findings.why_general: Grok exposes GROK_SESSION_ID while svc-ensure-worktree does not read it, and direct Cursor children can outlive or exit without releasing synthetic claims; every cross-host mutation can therefore collide with its own prior owner.
findings.harness_fix: Normalize GROK_SESSION_ID to SVC_SESSION_ID in the Grok SessionStart/wirer and add GROK_SESSION_ID to scripts/svc-ensure-worktree.mjs sessionId(); require the Cursor launch wrapper to mint a task-specific delegated child binding carrying parent session, PID/process-start token, and generation, then release or evidence-recover that binding on child exit.

findings.gap: Cursor agents were launched directly without a governed lifecycle channel, so captured stdout stayed empty while work and hook failures continued only in private Cursor logs.
findings.why_general: The canonical review launcher still has no Cursor transport, so operators must use raw cursor-agent --print and infer running, completed, failed, or hook-degraded state from PIDs, output artifacts, and /tmp/cursor-agent-logs-*.
findings.harness_fix: Add a first-class Cursor transport to scripts/run-external-review.mjs backed by a scripts/run-cursor-agent.mjs wrapper that emits a durable launch/status/result JSON, records PID and Cursor session-log path, streams or heartbeats when stdout is buffered, validates the requested artifact at process exit, and reports hook empty_stdout events as degraded or failed instead of silent progress.

findings.gap: The receipt checker accepts schema-v1 review envelopes on fresh commits, allowing manually written notes to bypass schema-v3 reviewer_evidence.
findings.why_general: The official emitter upgrades new review receipts to v3, but the consumer grandfathering is keyed only to the self-declared schema_version rather than the target commit's age, so any future Grok/Cursor run can attach a synthetic v1 note to a new SHA.
findings.harness_fix: In scripts/check-chain-receipts.mjs, bind legacy acceptance to a fixed rollout tag/cutoff commit and reject review-plan/review-exec schema_version below 3 for newer SHAs; keep scripts/emit-receipt.mjs as the sole new-note writer and add a migration helper that can upgrade legacy envelopes only from validated durable reviewer artifacts.

findings.gap: The land wrapper allowed PR and squash provenance to name WI-553 even though the frozen net tree contained none of WI-553's files.
findings.why_general: Squash merges can copy the branch's historical commit list into release text even when a commit's files are absent from the final tree; current landing checks bind head identity and review receipt but never reconcile named WIs to the net diff and manifest.
findings.harness_fix: Add a pre-merge provenance check in scripts/merge-pr-with-review-receipt.mjs that reads PR commits, files, frozen head tree, and manifest; require every WI named in title/body/squash text to have net-diff evidence or an explicit omitted/reverted disposition, and pass an explicit --subject/--body derived from the validated net change instead of accepting GitHub's historical auto-body.

findings.gap: Cursor model selection was pinned correctly, but the operator status loop exposed no authoritative usage-pool telemetry and encouraged reading an unrelated percentage bar.
findings.why_general: Cursor Models, Other Models/Auto, and BYOK are separate accounting surfaces, while raw cursor-agent status provides no run-bound pool percentage; the next delegated run will produce the same ambiguity even when the model argv is correct.
findings.harness_fix: Have scripts/run-cursor-agent.mjs read /home/dianast/.svc/cursor-exec-default.json and emit model, fast, usage_pool, and usage_percent_source in every launch/status record; when Cursor exposes no matching quota endpoint, report usage_percent as unavailable and explicitly reject inference from Other Models/Auto.

findings.gap: The shared chain-policy resolver fails closed safely but setup/worktree ensure does not perform or clearly drive its required one-time migration.
findings.why_general: Every clone upgraded to repository-shared policy can reach linked-worktree hooks before the git-common-dir file is seeded, producing the same refusal/noise and inviting ad hoc policy handling.
findings.harness_fix: Wire scripts/lib/chain-policy.mjs migrate-seed into setup and svc-ensure-worktree under a git-common-dir lock when exactly one trusted legacy or owner-home source exists; on ambiguity or no source, keep refusal but emit the exact migration command and source requirements in the worktree-ensure result.
